precepts.text: On the day of atonement ye shall afflict your souls: fasting, no eating and no drinking for the entire day, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.
precepts.point: Not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh: other translations read, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying, and sacrificing, yet they were still sexually indulgent all over the place. When it came to satisfying the flesh, they had no honor.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Colossians 2:23 speaks of “will worship, and humility, and neglecting of the body”. That goes back to verse 18, “in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels”: Paul has not changed the subject. Will worship is voluntary worship of what men say, humility here is humbling yourself to man, and neglecting of the body deals with fasting.

Leviticus shows the fast: “Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.” The tenth day of the seventh month is the day of atonement. To afflict your souls means to fast: no eating and no drinking for the entire 24-hour day.

And on that day you had to do what? Offer an offering made by fire. The fast and the sacrifice went together under the law. That is the “shew of wisdom” in Colossians 2:23: it has a show of wisdom because it is in the scriptures. It is there, but the sacrifice part of it was temporary.

precepts.text: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Leviticus 23 lays out the feasts of the Lord, seven of them in that chapter, and every single one of them represents Jesus Christ. The first annual one is the Lord’s passover, “In the fourteenth day of the first month at even”, the high holy day we just celebrated. So we go back to the instructions for the passover lamb.

“Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats”. Without blemish, a male of the first year. That is the lamb our forefathers had to choose.

That lamb without blemish is the pattern of Christ. The passover is a representation of Christ laying down his life for us, and everything spoken of the lamb in Exodus 12 points to him.

precepts.text: Ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot. Christ was that lamb.

The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Peter shows who that lamb without blemish was: “ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers; But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot”.

So Christ was that lamb without blemish, the same thing Exodus 12:5 required. Without blemish and without spot. He is the one “foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you”.

That is what John the Baptist said of Christ when he saw him coming: Behold the Lamb of God that takes away the sins of the world. The passover of Leviticus 23:5 is fulfilled in him.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Still in the passover instructions: “In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.”

Neither shall ye break a bone thereof. Those are the instructions for how to slaughter the lamb: do not break the bones of it.

That one command is going to be fulfilled to the letter in Christ. The high holy day of passover that we just went over is a picture of him, down to his bones.

precepts.text: He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken. The prophecy written of Christ.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Here is the prophecy about Christ: “He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.”

What was commanded for the passover lamb in Exodus 12:46, “neither shall ye break a bone thereof”, is written here as a prophecy of the Messiah. Not one of his bones would be broken.

The passover is a representation of Christ laying down his life for us, and the Psalms spoke it ahead of time, so that when it came to pass we would know he is our passover.

Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
This is the fulfilment. “The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken”.

“Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs”.

They broke the legs of the two crucified with him, but not his. Thus fulfilling the prophecy in Psalms 34:20, and the passover command, neither shall ye break a bone thereof. Christ was that passover lamb, and there is still more meat to scrape off the bones of this.

precepts.text: But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel. Article read in class: the unblemished passover lambs were raised at Migdal Eder, the tower of the flock by Bethlehem, wrapped in cloths, and brought to Jerusalem for sacrifice; the same road Christ walked, born in Bethlehem and offered at Jerusalem during Passover.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
The lambs without blemish were raised in Bethlehem and slaughtered in Jerusalem. Same thing as Jesus Christ. So the prophecy: “But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.”

Christ was born in Bethlehem. An article read in the class shows how our forefathers handled the passover lambs: the high priests given charge over them brought forth lambs without blemish from Migdal Eder in Bethlehem, wrapped in cloths, and brought them to Jerusalem for sacrifice. Migdal Eder means the tower of the flock, the same tower of the flock read about in Micah the fourth chapter, the eighth verse.

This Jesus was born in Bethlehem, wrapped in cloths, and eventually brought to Jerusalem during passover, where he offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins. The same road as the lambs.

precepts.text: She brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes: the same handling our forefathers gave the lambs brought to Jerusalem. Thus fulfilling prophecy; Christ is our passover.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:) To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child.”

To be taxed together you have to be married, brothers. You have to have papers, jointly. Not a toilet paper: years ago a brother wrote an instrument of divorce on toilet paper, because he did not really value her or count her as his wife.

“And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes”. They wrapped Christ in swaddling clothes, the same thing our forefathers did with the lambs when they brought them to Jerusalem.

Born in Bethlehem where the passover lambs were raised, wrapped the way they were wrapped, offered in Jerusalem at passover. Thus fulfilling prophecy. So we know Christ was our passover.

precepts.text: I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
After passover comes the next feast: “on the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread unto the Lord: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread.” There is that seven again.

The unleavened bread represents Christ: his sinless life, not having leaven. We know the history too, the Most High wanted us to hurry up and leave Egypt, so there was no time to sit and bake bread. But it also goes into Christ’s unleavened life, sinless and blameless.

Christ says it: “I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger”. He is the bread of life, the unleavened bread of the feast.

precepts.text: Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. The old leaven is sin.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”.

The old leaven is sin. Purge it out, that you may be a new lump. Because Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.

Christ was that unleavened bread that laid his life down for the children of Israel. So the passover and the feast of unleavened bread in Leviticus 23:5-6 both come to him: he is the lamb and he is the bread. With these the class counted three of the seven so far: the Sabbath, the passover, and the feast of unleavened bread.

precepts.text: Now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept. Every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming. The same promise stands for us if we believe and keep the commandments in the faith of Christ.
precepts.point: The feast of firstfruits: count seven sabbaths complete from the wave offering, and number fifty days. Seven sabbaths again, complete.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
The two wave loaves of Leviticus 23:17 “are the firstfruits unto the Lord.” Paul shows who the firstfruits are: “But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.” Christ is the firstfruits.

“For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.” Then the order is set: “But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.”

The same promise stands for us if we believe and keep the commandments in the faith of Christ: first Christ was raised, and afterward we that are his are raised at his coming.

Like the sabbath, the passover and the feast of unleavened bread before it, the feast of firstfruits is a representation of Christ. All seven of the high holy days read in Leviticus 23 represent Jesus Christ, and seven sabbaths counted “complete” to the fifty days points to completion in him.

precepts.text: Ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, waiting for the adoption, the redemption of our body.
precepts.point: The feast of firstfruits: count seven sabbaths complete from the wave offering, and number fifty days. Seven sabbaths again, complete.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Christ is the firstfruits, and his people are called firstfruits with him: “And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.”

Redemption of what body? The body that we used to have, when we were in the heavens with Christ. That is what we groan and wait for.

We are supposed to be the firstfruits: the crème de la crème, the best of the best, if we would repent in Christ. So the “firstfruits unto the Lord” brought out of Israel’s habitations in Leviticus 23:17 point not only to Christ risen, but to the Israelites who have his Spirit and wait for their redemption.

precepts.text: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
precepts.point: The feast of firstfruits: count seven sabbaths complete from the wave offering, and number fifty days. Seven sabbaths again, complete.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
James says it the same way: “Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.”

The Most High, of his own will, begat us with the word of truth for this purpose, that we should be a kind of firstfruits. We become that if we follow after Christ’s example, since Christ is the firstfruits risen from the dead.

So the feast of firstfruits in Leviticus 23:15-17, the new offering brought to the Lord after seven sabbaths complete, is a picture of Christ and of the people he begets by the word: the best of the best, offered unto the Lord.

precepts.text: These are they which were not defiled with women: not defiled with false doctrine and philosophy, and not defiled literally. These follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth, being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.
precepts.point: The feast of firstfruits: count seven sabbaths complete from the wave offering, and number fifty days. Seven sabbaths again, complete.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Revelation shows the firstfruits standing with Christ: “These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins.” Not defiled with philosophy, not defiled with false doctrine, and also not defiled with a literal woman.

“These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men, being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.” They follow Christ wherever he goes, and they are redeemed from among men.

This is the end of the feast of firstfruits in Leviticus 23: Christ the firstfruits risen, and afterward those that are his, kept clean from the world’s doctrine and its filth, offered as “the firstfruits unto the Lord.”

precepts.text: He shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds. The elect is Israel, the only people scattered from one end of heaven to the other.
precepts.point: The feast of trumpets: in the seventh month, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Why do we blow the trumpet? Because it was commanded of us, on the new moons and on our high holy days: “a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.” But like every one of these feasts, it is a representation of Christ.

Christ says: “And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” The trumpet sounds at his coming, and it gathers his elect.

The elect is only Israel, not all nations. They are gathered “from one end of heaven to the other” because we were scattered from one end of heaven to the other. That tells you who the children of God are: the only people scattered from one end of the earth to the other are the so-called blacks and Hispanics, the Israelites.

So the feast of trumpets looks forward to that great sound, when Christ sends his angels to gather his scattered people home.

precepts.text: The Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning, and the Lord GOD shall blow the trumpet. The Lord of hosts shall defend them, and the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.
precepts.point: The feast of trumpets: in the seventh month, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
That trumpet is not talking about a flute or some soft sound. When Christ comes back, everybody is going to fear. Zechariah shows it: “And the Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning: and the Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south.” This is when we are going to conquer the nations.

“The Lord of hosts shall defend them; and they shall devour, and subdue with sling stones”. We are going to devour all these nations, put them under our feet, break them in half. Then “they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine; and they shall be filled like bowls, and as the corners of the altar.”

“And the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.” The Most High said he is going to save us. That is some beautiful stuff right there.

So the memorial of blowing of trumpets in Leviticus 23:24 points to the day the Lord God himself blows the trumpet, defends Israel, and lifts his people up like the stones of a crown upon his land.

precepts.text: And the trumpet shall give a sound, which when every man heareth, they shall be suddenly afraid. That trumpet is no flute; it is a frightening sound.
precepts.point: The feast of trumpets: in the seventh month, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
The trumpet sound at Christ’s coming is no flute and no harmonica. Ezra says: “And the trumpet shall give a sound, which when every man heareth, they shall be suddenly afraid.”

That is how you know it is not talking about a soft sound or any instrument you could think of. Every man who hears it is suddenly afraid. That trumpet is a frightening sound.

It lines up with Matthew 24:31, the “great sound of a trumpet” that gathers the elect, and with Zechariah 9:14, where “the Lord God shall blow the trumpet” and his arrow goes forth as the lightning. The feast of trumpets in Leviticus 23:24-25 is a memorial pointing to that day: the gathering of Israel, and terror for the nations.

precepts.text: The priests under the law were many, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death; but this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. That is how Christ is able to save to the uttermost and atone continually: there is no death in him.
precepts.point: The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
The day of atonement, when Israel was to “afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord”, is a representation of Christ. Christ was that atonement.

“By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.” The better testament is the new covenant. “And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death”: the priests under the law died, one after another.

“But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him”. Christ is the true high priest, with no death in him. That is how he is able to atone for our sins continually, where the old priests could only atone until they died.

precepts.text: Not by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. He is the mediator of the new testament, as Moses was mediator when we came out of Egypt; and where a testament is, there must of necessity be the death of the testator. That is why Christ had to die: a testament is of force after men are dead, and while the testator lives it can still change.
precepts.point: The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.” His blood was given for atonement, and he died only once. Eternal redemption for whom? For us, the Israelites.

“For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” Without spot means blameless: he had no sin.

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament”, just as Moses was the mediator for us when we came up out of Egypt, so “that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” That promise is ours if we believe.

“For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.” For the testament to come to fruition and be valid, the testator had to die. That is why Christ had to die. “For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.” While a man is alive, his testament can still change. “Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.” Blood had to be spilled for the first covenant of animal sacrifice too. The yearly atonement of Leviticus 23:27 was fulfilled once for all in Christ’s own blood.

precepts.text: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood. Propitiation means atonement.
precepts.point: The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Paul names what Christ is: “Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood”. God sent Christ forth, and propitiation means atonement.

He was set forth “to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God”. The sins that are past are forgiven through faith in his blood, by God’s forbearance toward us.

So the day of atonement, when Israel afflicted their souls and brought an offering by fire, finds its meaning in Christ. He is the atonement God himself set forth, and we receive it through faith in his blood.

precepts.text: He is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world. That world is scattered Israel, all Israel, that they might have time to repent.
precepts.point: The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
John says it plainly: “And he is the propitiation for our sins”. Christ is the atonement for our sins, the fulfilment of the day of atonement in Leviticus 23:27.

Then: “and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.” That world is the scattered Israelites, all Israel, so that they may have time to repent. It is talking about Israel; it is not talking about all nations.

The next reading shows it: in the high priest’s long garment “was the whole world”, and that world was the twelve tribes. So when Christ atones for the world, he atones for Israel wherever they have been scattered.

precepts.text: For in the long garment was the whole world: the high priest's ephod carried a stone for each tribe. The world on Aaron's chest was Israel, and Christ is the new high priest.
precepts.point: The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Remember, Christ is the new high priest. Wisdom shows what the high priest carried: “For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and thy Majesty upon the diadem of his head.”

That is Aaron the high priest, and the long garment is the ephod. There was a stone for each tribe. The whole world on Aaron’s chest was Israel. It did not represent the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Hittites, the Perizzites or the Ishmaelites; only the Israelites.

That is how 1 John 2:2 is understood: Christ is “the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.” The world the high priest bore before God on the day of atonement was the twelve tribes, and the world Christ atones for as the new high priest is scattered Israel.

precepts.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us: Christ pitched his tent among us.
precepts.point: The feast of tabernacles, seven days unto the Lord. Tabernacle, sukkot, booth: it means to dwell.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord.” Another word for tabernacles is sukkot, booths, and it means to dwell.

John shows who the feast points to: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,)”. The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us: he pitched his tent among us. Christ walked among us.

So the feast of tabernacles, like the sabbath, the passover, unleavened bread, firstfruits, trumpets and atonement before it, is a representation of Christ. The seven days of dwelling in booths look to the Son of God coming to dwell with his people in the flesh.

precepts.text: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. They thought he meant the building of forty six years; but he spake of the temple of his body. His body was the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands.
precepts.point: The feast of tabernacles, seven days unto the Lord. Tabernacle, sukkot, booth: it means to dwell.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” The Jews took him simply: “Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?” They thought he meant the building.

“But he spake of the temple of his body.” His body is the temple, the tabernacle. Hebrews 9:11 shows it: “But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building”. His body was that greater and more perfect tabernacle. “Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.”

So the booths Israel dwelt in for the feast of tabernacles point to Christ’s own body, the true tabernacle in which God dwelt among us, destroyed and raised up again in three days.

precepts.text: Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. He is the God of Israel; that is the completion every feast was pointing to.
precepts.point: The feast of tabernacles, seven days unto the Lord. Tabernacle, sukkot, booth: it means to dwell.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them”. That is what tabernacle means: to dwell. He shall dwell with whom? The Israelites.

Then: “and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.” All praises to the Most High for that. He is not the God of the Ishmaelites, not the God of the Arabs, not the God of the white man. He is the God of Israel only.

This is the completion every feast was pointing to. All seven of the high holy days read in Leviticus 23, and there are more, represent Jesus Christ, and the feast of tabernacles ends where the scriptures end: God dwelling with his people Israel for ever.

precepts.text: The feasts of the Lord, starting with the Sabbath, are his appointed times.
precepts.point: The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
The moon serves “in her season for a declaration of times”. Leviticus 23 shows what those times are: “Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.” Convocations means gatherings.

The first holy day God tells Moses to list is the Sabbath: “Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest”, instituted from Genesis 2. Then: “These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.” He did not say seasons for the Sabbath, because the Sabbath is all year round. The ones that follow are seasonal holy days.

“In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover”, in the spring. Then the feast of unleavened bread on the fifteenth day; Pentecost, counting fifty days; “In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets”, which is the seventh new moon celebration; the day of atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month; and “The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles”.

So the “declaration of times” is the high holy days. “From the moon is the sign of feasts”: every feast is counted from the new moon, when it is in its brightness, because that is how it was in the kingdom.

precepts.text: The seventh day is a sabbath of rest, an holy convocation in all your dwellings; Exodus 16:29 does not undo the gathering.
precepts.point: For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation: you may have to travel and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area. The first assemblies met in houses, and that is how camps start; a man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth, and the Lord honors that faith.

note.label: Exodus 16: Manna From Heaven and the Sabbath Proved

precepts.why:
“abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.” That is about not going out to gather food on the sabbath; some of the people had gone out on the seventh day to gather and found none. Some foolish Israelites read verse 29 out of context and say you never have to leave your house or join a congregation on the sabbath. That is not what it says.

The sabbath is a holy convocation. “Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation; ye shall do no work therein: it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.” A holy convocation is a large gathering, and it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings, so we are to come together on it. Exodus 16:29 does not undo the gathering; it stops the going out to gather food.

precepts.text: One day excels another by the knowledge of the Lord: some days He made high days and hallowed them, and some He made ordinary.
precepts.point: It is a holy convocation, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.” The Most High gave us holy days, and He Himself proclaimed them. “Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun? By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.”

“Some of them hath he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.” The Passover, Tabernacles, the new moon and the Sabbath are the high days He made; the days He did not name are ordinary days.

So a holiday not listed in this Bible and not ordained of the Most High has nothing holy about it. Only His knowledge distinguishes one day from another.

precepts.text: On the holy sabbath day whosoever doeth work shall be put to death, and ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations; no cooking on the Sabbath.
precepts.point: It is a holy convocation, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation; ye shall do no work therein.” Moses gave the same word to all the congregation: “Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be to you an holy day, a sabbath of rest to the Lord: whosoever doeth work therein shall be put to death.”

Then more than no working: “Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.” So there is no cooking on the Sabbath. Keeping it holy is more than staying off the job.

And it is “the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.” No matter where your dwelling is, Israel, North America, London or Australia, the Sabbath is still the Sabbath: Friday sundown to Saturday sundown in whatever time zone you are in.

precepts.text: If the people of the land bring ware or victuals on the sabbath day to sell, we would not buy it of them; no buying and no selling on the Sabbath.
precepts.point: It is a holy convocation, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
Keeping the Sabbath holy is also no buying and no selling. Israel covenanted: “if the people of the land bring ware or any victuals on the sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day.”

So on the Sabbath there is no work, no kindling fire to cook, and no buying and selling. And it is “an holy convocation”, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate.

precepts.text: The feast of unleavened bread is called the Passover; the two feasts run together as one.
precepts.point: On the last day of unleavened bread you may also cook, unless it falls on the seventh day Sabbath. The only time you can cook on the seventh day Sabbath is when the Passover falls on that day, because you cannot have the Passover without the lamb roast with fire; no other high holy day gives you a set meal, and no other feast overrides the Sabbath cooking prohibition.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover. And on the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread unto the Lord.” The fourteenth day at even means the fifteenth day, so both verses are saying the same thing: the first day of the Passover is also the first day of the feast of unleavened bread.

Luke shows the two run together as one: “Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.” The feast of unleavened bread is called the Passover.

On the first day and the seventh day is an holy convocation, no buying, no selling, no servile work. But you can cook on the Passover, because there is no Passover without the Passover meal: the lamb, unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

precepts.text: In the days of Josias the feast of unleavened bread is called the feast of sweet bread, kept seven days with the passover.
precepts.point: On the last day of unleavened bread you may also cook, unless it falls on the seventh day Sabbath. The only time you can cook on the seventh day Sabbath is when the Passover falls on that day, because you cannot have the Passover without the lamb roast with fire; no other high holy day gives you a set meal, and no other feast overrides the Sabbath cooking prohibition.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
In the days of king Josias the feast has another name: “the children of Israel which were present held the passover at that time, and the feast of sweet bread seven days.” The feast of sweet bread is the feast of unleavened bread, kept seven days with the passover, just as Leviticus 23 sets it: “seven days ye must eat unleavened bread.”

On the last day of unleavened bread you may also cook, unless it falls on the seventh day Sabbath. The only time you can cook on the seventh day Sabbath is when the Passover falls on that day, because you cannot have the Passover without the lamb roast with fire. No other high holy day gives you a set meal, and no other feast overrides the Sabbath cooking prohibition.

precepts.text: Pentecost is the holy feast of the seven weeks, the seven sabbaths counted after the wave sheaf.
precepts.point: The meat offerings and drink offerings and carnal ordinances were a figure for the time then present, imposed until the time of reformation; they could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience. But Christ being come, an high priest of good things to come, Christ is now in place of all those oblations and sacrifices.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
From the morrow after the sabbath, from the day the sheaf of the wave offering was brought, “seven sabbaths shall be complete”, seven times seven which is forty and nine, and “the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days.” That is why the feast is called Pentecost, from fifty, as a pentagon has five sides.

Tobit calls it by both names: “in the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy feast of the seven weeks.” It is also the feast of weeks, because of the seven weeks, the seven sabbaths, that are counted after the wave sheaf.

precepts.text: Let no man judge you in meat or in drink or in respect of an holyday; no man may condemn you for keeping the holy days without the sacrifices, now that Christ is come.
precepts.point: The meat offerings and drink offerings and carnal ordinances were a figure for the time then present, imposed until the time of reformation; they could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience. But Christ being come, an high priest of good things to come, Christ is now in place of all those oblations and sacrifices.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
With the two wave loaves came burnt offerings, a sin offering and peace offerings, “with their meat offering, and their drink offerings.” That is what Colossians is talking about: “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days.”

Those who did not believe in Christ condemned the followers of Christ as wicked for not sacrificing on the holy days. We still keep the holy days, but we do not offer the offerings, because the body of Christ has been given. No man may judge you for keeping the holyday without the meat and drink offerings, now that Christ is come.

precepts.text: The gifts and sacrifices were a figure for the time then present, carnal ordinances imposed until the time of reformation; Christ being come stands in place of them.
precepts.point: The meat offerings and drink offerings and carnal ordinances were a figure for the time then present, imposed until the time of reformation; they could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience. But Christ being come, an high priest of good things to come, Christ is now in place of all those oblations and sacrifices.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
The offerings of Pentecost, the lambs, the bullock, the rams, the kid of the goats, the meat offering and the drink offerings, were “a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience.”

They “stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.” They had a set time.

“But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands”: Christ is now in place of all those oblations and sacrifices. The holy convocation of Pentecost stands, a statute for ever; the sacrifices are fulfilled in him.

precepts.text: The moon serves for a declaration of times, and from the moon is the sign of feasts; the month is called after her name.
precepts.point: If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets.” The first day of the month is the new moon, so the memorial of blowing of trumpets is a new moon; the seventh new moon is the special one, and that one is called the memorial of blowing of trumpets.

The Most High “made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world. From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.” The moon is needed to calculate the feasts. “The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing”: the new moon starts the new month, and she increases through her phases.

If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

precepts.text: The lights in the firmament were made for signs and for seasons, the lesser light to rule the night, on the fourth day; the moon came after the week was already counting.
precepts.point: If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
The moon governs the months and the feasts, but it has nothing to do with the seventh day Sabbath. The lights in the firmament were made “for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”, “the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night”, and “the evening and the morning were the fourth day.”

The moon was not created on the first day of the week but on the fourth. The week was already counting, day one, day two, day three, before the moon existed. So the moon cannot set the Sabbath; the seven day rotation has run since the first day and nothing changes it.

The day starts at evening, for the evening and the morning were the day; darkness was here first and has seniority. The Sabbath will always be Friday sundown to Saturday sundown.

precepts.text: The heavens and the earth were finished, and on the seventh day God ended his work and rested; the moon made on the fourth day did not dictate the seventh day Sabbath.
precepts.point: If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them. And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it.”

The heavens and the earth were finished, moon included, and the Most High still rested on the seventh day. The moon made on the fourth day did not dictate the seventh day Sabbath; the count of seven did, running from the first day.

So the memorial of blowing of trumpets is reckoned by the new moon, but the Sabbath stands on its own seven day rotation, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown, always.

precepts.text: Let neither man nor beast taste any thing, nor feed, nor drink water; that is the affliction of the soul, tasting nothing at all.
precepts.point: From even unto even shall ye celebrate your sabbath, the ninth day of the month at even. Even unto even is how days are numbered, one complete day of twenty-four hours, not sunrise to sunrise, for the evening and the morning were the first day.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
On the tenth day of this seventh month, the same month as the blowing of trumpets, is the day of atonement, and “ye shall afflict your souls.” What is afflicting the soul? Nineveh shows it: “Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water.”

No eating, no drinking, no tasting anything at all. That goes for gum, because you can taste gum, and even toothpaste: the last thing you do before the fast begins is brush your teeth before the sun goes down, and the first thing after it ends is brush them after the sun goes down. If you can taste it, keep it out of your mouth.

It is serious: “whatsoever soul it be that shall not be afflicted in that same day, he shall be cut off from among his people”, and whoever does any work that day, “the same soul will I destroy from among his people.”

precepts.text: The evening and the morning were the first day; the day starts at evening, so the sabbath runs from even unto even.
precepts.point: From even unto even shall ye celebrate your sabbath, the ninth day of the month at even. Even unto even is how days are numbered, one complete day of twenty-four hours, not sunrise to sunrise, for the evening and the morning were the first day.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“in the ninth day of the month at even, from even unto even, shall ye celebrate your sabbath.” Even unto even is how days are numbered: “And the evening and the morning were the first day.”

The day starts at evening. So the day of atonement is one complete day of twenty-four hours from sundown on the ninth to sundown on the tenth, not sunrise to sunrise, and every sabbath runs the same way, from even unto even.

precepts.text: The fifteenth day of the seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days; the first day an holy convocation, and the eighth day a solemn assembly with no servile work.
precepts.point: Leviticus 23 shows what this feast is: all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that the Most High made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when he brought them out of the land of Egypt. That is why once a year, around October, you will see us out in the wilderness in tents, eight days counting the solemn assembly, those of us able to get the time off; all our feast days are memorials of what the Lord did for us.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
“And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month ye shall have an holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work, and ye shall keep a feast unto the Lord seven days.” Leviticus 23 names this feast.

“The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord. On the first day shall be an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein. Seven days ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord: on the eighth day shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord: it is a solemn assembly; and ye shall do no servile work therein.”

The feast of tabernacles: the first day an holy convocation, seven days of offerings made by fire, of which the thirteen bullocks, two rams, and fourteen lambs of Numbers 29 are the first day's, and the eighth day a solemn assembly with no servile work. That is why our time in the wilderness is eight days counting the solemn assembly.

precepts.text: A statute for ever in your generations: ye shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when I brought them out of Egypt.
precepts.point: Leviticus 23 shows what this feast is: all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that the Most High made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when he brought them out of the land of Egypt. That is why once a year, around October, you will see us out in the wilderness in tents, eight days counting the solemn assembly, those of us able to get the time off; all our feast days are memorials of what the Lord did for us.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
Leviticus 23 shows what the feast of the fifteenth day of the seventh month is. “And ye shall keep it a feast unto the Lord seven days in the year. It shall be a statute for ever in your generations: ye shall celebrate it in the seventh month. Ye shall dwell in booths seven days; all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths.”

“That your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.” A statute for ever in your generations, so that your generations may know what the Most High did when He brought Israel out of Egypt.

That is why once a year, around October, you will see us out in the wilderness in tents, eight days counting the solemn assembly, those of us able to get the time off. All our feast days are memorials of what the Lord did for us.

precepts.text: Count from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day the wave sheaf is brought; seven sabbaths shall be complete; the counting law behind the feast of weeks.
precepts.point: Rejoice before the Most High, thou and thy son and thy daughter, thy manservant and thy maidservant, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow; and remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt.

note.label: Deuteronomy 16: The Three Feasts and Just Judgment

precepts.why:
“Seven weeks shalt thou number unto thee: begin to number the seven weeks from such time as thou beginnest to put the sickle to the corn.” Leviticus gives the counting law behind it: “And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete”.

The count begins from the day the wave sheaf is brought, when the sickle first goes to the corn, and runs seven sabbaths, seven weeks. Another name for the feast of weeks is the feast of firstfruits: you count seven weeks and then a day, fifty days, which is Pentecost.

Then keep the feast unto the Most High with a tribute of a freewill offering according as the Lord thy God hath blessed thee, and rejoice before him, thou and thy son and thy daughter, thy manservant and thy maidservant, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow; and remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt.

precepts.text: In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, the day being reckoned from even to even.
precepts.point: Solomon confessed that the house he built was great, for great is our God above all gods, yet the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Him. He asked Huram for a cunning man to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, and colored cloth, and for cedar, fir, and algum trees out of Lebanon, promising wheat, barley, wine, and oil to the hewers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover.”

At even: the day is reckoned from even to even. So the passover is kept at even on the fourteenth, and the feast of unleavened bread begins the fifteenth day. These are among the solemn feasts Solomon named, ordained forever to Israel.

precepts.text: Israel is commanded to dwell in booths seven days so their generations may know the Most High made them dwell in booths when He brought them out of Egypt.
precepts.point: On the second day the chief of the fathers, the priests, and the Levites gather to Ezra to understand the words of the law, and they find written that Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month.

note.label: Nehemiah 8: Ezra Reads the Law at the Water Gate

precepts.why:
When the chief of the fathers, the priests, and the Levites gathered to Ezra on the second day to understand the words of the law, this is what they found written: “Ye shall dwell in booths seven days; all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths.”

The law gives the reason with the commandment: “That your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.” The feast of the seventh month is a memorial. Every generation of Israel dwells in booths so it may know that the Most High made the children of Israel dwell in booths when He brought them out of Egypt.

That is why the people went forth for branches and made themselves booths on their roofs, in their courts, in the courts of the house of God and in the streets, and sat under them. They were doing what was written, as it had not been done since the days of Joshua, and Ezra read in the book of the law day by day until the solemn assembly.

precepts.text: Count fifty days after the Sabbath and offer a new meat offering of two wave loaves, the first fruits unto the Most High, which is Pentecost.
precepts.point: Pentecost comes from penta, meaning fifty, the fiftieth day counted from the Sabbath after Passover. It is also called the Feast of Weeks and the first fruits, and Israel kept it through every captivity, Assyrian, Babylonian, and Greek.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.” The disciples were keeping the feast, which confounds the claim that after Christ died the law was done away with. If the ceremonial law was nailed to the cross, why did the disciples keep gathering for Pentecost?

Pentecost comes from penta, meaning fifty, the fiftieth day counted from the Sabbath after Passover: “ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete: Even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days; and ye shall offer a new meat offering unto the Lord.”

“Ye shall bring out of your habitations two wave loaves”, “they are the firstfruits unto the Lord.” That is why it is also called the Feast of Weeks and the first fruits. The law remained in effect after his death, and the disciples continued keeping the feast days written in Leviticus 23.

The Most High gave us holy days; a holiday not listed in this Bible and not ordained of the Most High has nothing holy about it. By the knowledge of the Lord the days were distinguished: some He made high days, as the Passover, Tabernacles, the new moon, and the Sabbath, and the days He did not name are ordinary days.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: Six days shall work be done, but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation. No matter where your dwelling is, Israel, North America, London, or Australia, the Sabbath is still the Sabbath: Friday sundown to Saturday sundown in whatever time zone you are in.

Keeping the Sabbath holy is more than no working. Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day, so there is no cooking on the Sabbath; and if the people of the land bring ware or victuals on the sabbath day to sell, we would not buy it of them, so there is no buying and no selling.

It is a holy convocation, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover. The fourteenth day at even means the fifteenth day, so the verse about the fifteenth day is saying the same thing: the first day of the Passover is also the first day of the feast of unleavened bread.

On the last day of unleavened bread you may also cook, unless it falls on the seventh day Sabbath. The only time you can cook on the seventh day Sabbath is when the Passover falls on that day, because you cannot have the Passover without the lamb roast with fire; no other high holy day gives you a set meal, and no other feast overrides the Sabbath cooking prohibition.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: On the first day and on the seventh day is an holy convocation: no buying, no selling, no servile work. But you can cook on the Passover, because there is no Passover without the Passover meal, the lamb, unleavened bread, and bitter herbs.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: When ye be come into the land, ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest, and he shall wave the sheaf before the Lord on the morrow after the sabbath, with an he lamb without blemish for a burnt offering.
This wave sheaf day is what the New Testament calls the preparation: after the Passover was kept, the day following was the preparation, which prepared for this feast of the waving of the sheaf.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: Ye shall eat neither bread nor parched corn nor green ears until the selfsame day that ye have brought an offering unto your God; it is a statute for ever throughout your generations.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: From the morrow after the sabbath, from the day the sheaf of the wave offering was brought, count seven sabbaths complete, seven times seven which is forty and nine, and the morrow after the seventh sabbath is the fiftieth day. That is why the feast is called Pentecost, from fifty, as a pentagon has five sides; it is also called the feast of weeks, because of the seven weeks that are counted.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: With the two wave loaves came burnt offerings, a sin offering, and peace offerings, meat offerings and drink offerings. That is what Colossians is talking about when it says let no man judge you in meat or in drink or in respect of an holyday: those who did not believe in Christ condemned the followers of Christ as wicked for not sacrificing on the holy days. We still keep the holy days, but we do not offer the offerings, because the body of Christ has been given.

The meat offerings and drink offerings and carnal ordinances were a figure for the time then present, imposed until the time of reformation; they could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience. But Christ being come, an high priest of good things to come, Christ is now in place of all those oblations and sacrifices.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: When ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not make clean riddance of the corners of thy field, neither gather the gleaning of thy harvest: thou shalt leave them unto the poor and to the stranger.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, is a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets. The new moon starts the new month, so the memorial of blowing of trumpets is a new moon; the seventh new moon is the special one, and that one is called the memorial of blowing of trumpets.

But the moon has nothing to do with the seventh day Sabbath. The day starts at evening, for the evening and the morning were the first day; darkness was here first and has seniority. The moon was not even created on the first day of the week but on the fourth day, and the heavens and the earth were finished and the Most High still rested on the seventh day. The seven day rotation has run since the first day and nothing changes it; the Sabbath will always be Friday sundown to Saturday sundown.
If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: On the tenth day of this seventh month, the same month as the blowing of trumpets, is the day of atonement, an holy convocation; ye shall afflict your souls, and do no manner of work in that same day, for whatsoever soul does any work that same day, that soul will the Most High destroy from among his people.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: To afflict your soul is to neither feed nor drink water nor taste anything, as Nineveh was commanded: no eating, no drinking, no tasting anything at all. That goes for gum, because you can taste gum, and even toothpaste; the last thing you do before the fast begins is brush your teeth before the sun goes down, and the first thing after it ends is brush them after the sun goes down. If you can taste it, keep it out of your mouth.

From even unto even shall ye celebrate your sabbath, the ninth day of the month at even. Even unto even is how days are numbered, one complete day of twenty-four hours, not sunrise to sunrise, for the evening and the morning were the first day.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: The fifteenth day of the seventh month is the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord. The first day is an holy convocation with no servile work, and on the eighth day is an holy convocation, a solemn assembly.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: Ye shall take you on the first day the boughs of goodly trees, branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook, and rejoice before the Lord your God seven days. Those branches may be collected and put together in a vase in the home for the feast.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

points: Ye shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that the Most High made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when He brought them out of the land of Egypt, as when Israel was in the wilderness dwelling in tents.
